title: Why society takes up new science
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:59Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Why society takes up new science
card: Science can show that a practice works, but people do not always adopt it. Several factors affect whether a community takes it up.
Cost and evidence matter. A practice is more likely to spread if it is affordable and if the evidence that it works is strong.
Trust and culture matter. People may avoid a practice if they distrust the source of the information, or if it clashes with their beliefs or customs.
Government support can make a practice easier to adopt. For example, a rebate can lower the price of solar panels, and council recycling bins make recycling simple.
draft.remember: People adopt new science for many reasons, not only because it works: cost, trust, culture and government support all play a part.

a.q: Tom's town has strong evidence that rainwater tanks save water. Few households buy one. Which reason fits best?
opts: The tanks cost more than most households want to pay
The evidence about tanks has been shown to be false
The government has paid for a tank for every household
Scientists have not tested whether tanks save water
a.why: Cost can stop people from adopting a practice even when the evidence is strong. The other options contradict the facts given: the evidence is strong, so it was not shown to be false or left untested, and few households buy, so it is not free.
a.clue: The evidence is already strong, so look at another factor.

b.q: A council offers free recycling bins and clear advice. Many residents still do not use them, saying they distrust the council's claims. Which factor explains this?
opts: Low trust in the source of the information
High cost of taking part in the program
Too little government support for recycling
b.why: The residents say they distrust the council, so trust is the factor at work. Government support is tempting, but the council has already provided bins and advice, so support is not what is missing.
b.clue: Read what the residents say about the council.

a.best: The tanks cost more than most households want to pay

b.best: Low trust in the source of the information
